appStorePromo: Version 0.1.0, the first release. Ten conversions, batches of any size, nine languages, no account and no paywall. The source and the issue tracker are public.
appStoreDescription:
Kitefold converts images and PDFs on your device. No account, no uploads, no subscription, and no limit on how many files you convert.

WHAT IT DOES

HEIC to JPG. iPhone photos that anything can open.
WebP to JPG. Saved images that will not open elsewhere.
PNG to JPG. Smaller files, with a background colour you pick.
Compress image. Give it a maximum file size and it finds the quality that lands just under your limit.
Resize image. Presets for email, social, screens and print, or a size you type.
Image to PDF. Many photos, one document, with a page size, margin and images per page.
PDF to JPG. Every page as an image, at the resolution you choose.
Merge PDF. Combine documents and reorder them before it runs.
Split PDF. Pull out page ranges, or break a document up every few pages.
Compress PDF. A smaller file, and a plain account of what that costs.

Any of these will run across a whole batch. Rename the results with tokens for the original name, a number, the date or the format. Save settings you use often as a preset. A history on the device lists what you converted and what it saved.

NOTHING IS UPLOADED

Most converters are either a website that takes your photos to somebody else's server, or an app that puts basic conversion behind a subscription. This one is neither, and it does not ask to be trusted on that.

There is no server and no networking code. There is no account and no sign in. There is no analytics, no advertising and no crash reporting SDK, and a check in the build fails if any package that collects data is ever added.

Kitefold picks up files through the system photo and file pickers, so it holds no permission to read your library. The only permission it can ask you for is notifications, so a long batch can show its progress while you are in another app. Refusing it does not stop a conversion.

The privacy label on this listing says No Data Collected. That is not a summary of a longer policy. It is the whole of it.

FREE, WITH NO LIMITS

Every conversion is free. No paid tier, no trial, no watermark, no cap on files, and no billing code in the app.

IT TELLS YOU WHAT HAPPENED

Converting sometimes makes a file bigger. Flat artwork encodes worse as JPG than as PNG, and it happens more often than people expect. When it does, Kitefold says the file grew, by how much, and why, rather than reporting nothing saved.

Before a batch runs, the estimated output size is measured on one of your real files instead of guessed from the input.

ALSO WORTH KNOWING

Share images or PDFs to Kitefold from any app, and convert them in the share sheet without opening it.
A batch keeps going when you leave the app, and cancelling keeps the files that already finished.
Nine languages: English, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Japanese, Chinese and Arabic, laid out right to left where that is how it reads.
Light and dark, following your device.
Works on iPhone and iPad.

Made by Owais Khan. The source is public, and so is the licence.

playFullDescription:
Kitefold converts images and PDFs on your phone. Nothing is uploaded, and that is enforced by Android rather than promised: the release build ships without the INTERNET permission, so the system refuses the app a network connection whatever its code asks for. Automatic Backup is off as well, so nothing is copied to Drive.

WHAT IT DOES

HEIC to JPG. Photos from an iPhone that anything can open.
WebP to JPG. Saved images that will not open elsewhere.
PNG to JPG. Smaller files, with a background colour you pick.
Compress image. Give it a maximum file size and it finds the quality that lands just under your limit.
Resize image. Presets for email, social, screens and print, or a size you type.
Image to PDF. Many photos, one document, with a page size, margin and images per page.
PDF to JPG. Every page as an image, at the resolution you choose.
Merge PDF. Combine documents and reorder them before it runs.
Split PDF. Pull out page ranges, or break a document up every few pages.
Compress PDF. A smaller file, and a plain account of what that costs.

Any of these will run across a whole batch. Rename the results with tokens for the original name, a number, the date or the format. Save settings you use often as a preset. A history on the device lists what you converted and what it saved.

THE PERMISSIONS IT ASKS FOR

Four, and you can check them on this page. A foreground service and its data sync type, so a long batch survives you leaving the app. Notifications, so that batch can show progress, and it is the only one you are ever asked about. Refusing it does not stop a conversion, it only means there is no notification. Vibration, for the tap when a conversion finishes.

There is no storage permission and no media permission, because files come in through the system picker, which runs outside the app and hands over only what you selected. And there is no internet permission, which is the point.

NO ACCOUNT, NO TRACKING, NO PAYWALL

There is no server and no networking code. There is no sign in. There is no analytics, no advertising and no crash reporting SDK, and a check in the build fails if any package that collects data is ever added.

Every conversion is free. No paid tier, no trial, no watermark, no cap on files, and no billing code in the app.

IT TELLS YOU WHAT HAPPENED

Converting sometimes makes a file bigger. Flat artwork encodes worse as JPG than as PNG, and it happens more often than people expect. When it does, Kitefold says the file grew, by how much, and why, rather than reporting nothing saved.

Before a batch runs, the estimated output size is measured on one of your real files instead of guessed from the input.

ALSO WORTH KNOWING

Share images or PDFs to Kitefold from any app and it opens ready to convert them.
A batch keeps going when you leave the app, and cancelling keeps the files that already finished.
Nine languages: English, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Japanese, Chinese and Arabic, laid out right to left where that is how it reads.

releaseNotes:
Version 0.1.0. The first release.

Ten conversions: HEIC, WebP and PNG to JPG, compress an image to a size limit, resize, images to PDF, PDF pages to images, and merge, split or compress a PDF. Batches of any size, renaming, presets and a local history. Nine languages.

All of it runs on the device, and none of it costs anything. If something is wrong, the issue tracker is the fastest way to tell me.
